facts: One arm's per-opportunity revenue, as sums: `n` opportunities (no-fills included, at revenue 0), `sum` = sum of revenue r_i and `sumSquares` = sum of r_i^2, all in one unit (cents). Sums add across days and placements, so rollup rows combine by addition before this is called.
Standard error of `value`.
Unrounded mean and standard error, per 1,000 opportunities.

Mean revenue per 1,000 opportunities with a 95% normal (CLT) interval. The sample variance comes from the sums, (Q - S^2/n) / (n - 1), clamped at 0 against rounding. Treats opportunities as independent, which ignores clustering by user: read the interval as a lower bound on the true width.

ai.title: Add revenue per thousand and uplift stats to shared statistics
ai.summary: New `revenuePerThousand` and `revenueUplift` functions in `common/src/util/stats.ts` compute mean revenue per 1,000 opportunities with 95% confidence intervals and ranked-vs-uniform uplift metrics from `RevenueSums` inputs. The `revenueUplift` function returns both a difference interval using independent-arm standard errors and a ratio interval via the delta method on the log scale, with the ratio null when either arm's mean is zero. These additions support ad-serving experiment readouts, complementing the existing Wilson interval and Newcombe difference utilities in the same module.
ai.evidence: The diff adds `revenuePerThousand` and `revenueUplift` functions, along with `RevenueSums`, `RevenuePerThousand`, and `RevenueUplift` types, to `common/src/util/stats.ts` for analyzing per-opportunity ad revenue in experiments.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show which experiment readout or Postgres query calls these new functions at this revision.

eli5.text: The shared statistics tool now includes two new calculations that measure advertising revenue per thousand opportunities and compare a targeted ad approach against a random one. These additions are part of the internal systems used to evaluate ad-serving experiments and do not alter how the app behaves for you. Since no reporting feature or dashboard currently uses these new numbers, you will see no change in your daily experience or account settings.

ai.title: Add user id minter constant to identity backend config
ai.summary: A new IdentityUserIdMinter type, IDENTITY_USER_ID_MINTER constant, and identityUserIdMinter() accessor were added to `common/src/constants/identity-backend.ts`. The constant defaults to `convex`, meaning new accounts still receive their user ids from the Convex sign-in mutation. This addition prepares the codebase for a future flip to `freebuff_web`, which would mint ids locally in Convex's format without a Convex call. The change is currently inert because no visible reader enforces the new constant yet.
ai.evidence: The diff adds a new type IdentityUserIdMinter, a constant IDENTITY_USER_ID_MINTER, and a function identityUserIdMinter to common/src/constants/identity-backend.ts, with IDENTITY_USER_ID_MINTER set to 'convex'.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show when or if the constant will be flipped to `freebuff_web` or which specific Convex functions must be cleared before that flip can occur.

eli5.text: The team added a new control switch that determines how unique account numbers are created when you sign in, preparing the system to soon stop using one external service for that task. This update is entirely internal infrastructure work for the Freebuff engineering team and does not change how the application behaves for you. Nothing visible happens today because the new switch is currently set to keep the old method active, so your existing account data and login experience remain exactly the same.
